newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kinkel urges Milosevic to recognise election wins.
newsitem.headline: Kinkel urges Milosevic to recognise election wins.

text.p: Germany's Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel called on Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic on Monday to recognise opposition victories in local elections last November.

Kinkel was speaking on Orthodox Christmas Eve, when Serbian pro-democracy demonstrators have vowed to defy a government ban and protest for the 50th straight day against the annulment of opposition election victories.
The German minister warned Milosevic that refusal to admit his Socialist party's defeat in 15 of the country's 18 largest cities, including Belgrade, could mean Yugoslavia's isolation within Europe.
"Mr Milosevic, you must recognise all opposition victories immediately," Kinkel said at a congress of the liberal Free Democrat Party (FDP) in the southern city of Stuttgart.
The Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) has verified opposition claims to have won in 15 cities.

Milosevic's Socialist government grudgingly admitted last week that the Zajedno (Together) opposition coalition had won in a few of the smaller cities but said that in other districts no party gained a majority or the results needed further study.
The Serbian Orthodox Church celebrates Christmas on January 7, according to the old Julian calendar.
